items.title: 11.3 Reaction mechanism and modes of bond breaking

source_refs.note: Topic 11.3 with Figures 11.5 and 11.6, printed pages 251-252.

blocks.title: Reaction mechanism
blocks.text: A reaction mechanism is the series of steps that take place in the course of the overall reaction. Like all chemical reactions, organic reactions involve the breaking of chemical bonds, and covalent bonds can break in two ways.

Homolytic fission occurs when the covalent bond breaks evenly to produce free radicals (Figure 11.5). A free radical is a species that contains an unpaired electron and is very reactive, because of the tendency of unpaired electrons to become paired. Heterolytic fission occurs when the covalent bond breaks in such a way that the originally shared pair of electrons is gained by one atom only, and oppositely charged ions are produced (Figure 11.6); this bond fission is shown by full curly arrows in mechanisms.

blocks.alt: Two reactions. A-B splits so that each atom keeps one of the two bonding electrons, shown by two fish-hook arrows, giving the free radicals A dot and B dot. In light (hv) Cl-Cl splits the same way into two chlorine free radicals.
blocks.caption: Homolytic fission and free radical formation (original diagram after Figure 11.5).

blocks.alt: Two reactions. A curly arrow moves the bonding pair of A-B to B, giving the ions A+ and B- (B is more electronegative). In CH3-Cl the pair moves to chlorine, giving a methyl carbocation CH3+ and a chloride ion Cl-.
blocks.caption: Heterolytic fission and formation of ions (original diagram after Figure 11.6).
Two modes of bond fission
rows: Cl-Cl with UV light gives 2 Cl radicals

blocks.prompt: Differentiate homolytic from heterolytic fission (exercise Q.2b).
blocks.explanation: In homolytic fission the shared pair splits one electron to each fragment, giving neutral free radicals with unpaired electrons, as when chlorine is split by light. In heterolytic fission both electrons go to the more electronegative atom, giving a cation and an anion, shown by a full curly arrow.

items: Mechanism = the steps of a reaction. Homolytic fission: bond splits evenly to free radicals (unpaired electron, very reactive). Heterolytic fission: both electrons to one atom, giving oppositely charged ions (full curly arrows).
